designSummary: Weekly run charts of time on high flow with pre-specified rules, plus p-charts and a stopping rule for safety balancing measures.
sampleSize: About 5 to 8 infants aged 8 weeks or older start high flow each week in season, about 90 over 20 weeks. Weekly medians from so few infants are noisy, so the chart uses two-week medians when a week has fewer than four infants. A fall from about 52 to 32 hours would give a shift of six or more points below the baseline median within the second cycle. For safety, 90 trials off give a 95 percent upper limit of about 18 percent if 10 percent re-escalate; the stopping rule (more than 15 percent over any four weeks, at least 12 trials off) is reviewed by the PICU lead rather than tested.
primaryAnalysis: Run chart of median hours on high flow with the baseline season's median as centre line and shift, trend and runs rules fixed in advance.
secondaryAnalysis: p-chart of re-escalation; counts of PICU transfers and 7-day readmissions; run chart of length of stay; adherence by day and night; descriptive outcomes for infants under 8 weeks on stepwise weaning.
missingData: Infants with missing stop times are traced in the chart by the ward clerk; any still missing are reported, not imputed.
multiplicity: One outcome measure carries the aim; balancing measures drive the stopping rule, not significance tests.
software: Spreadsheet run chart template kept by the ward's QI nurse and checked by the hospitalist lead.
overfittingGuards: Run chart and stopping rules fixed before November
Two-week medians used whenever a week has fewer than four infants
No subgroup testing beyond the age groups fixed by the protocol
summary: About 90 infants over the season; run chart rules for the aim and a pre-specified safety stopping rule.
